newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU barley sale said worth $136/T - traders.
newsitem.headline: EU barley sale said worth $136/T - traders.

text.p: A European Union sale of 235,300 tonnes of free-market barley is worth some $136 per tonne, on world markets, grain traders said on Thursday.
The EU's cereals management committee granted the barley at a maximum refund of 30.98 Ecus per tonne.
The sale is slightly above the average Fob price of a recent sale of optional-origin feed barley to Saudi Arabia, traders said.
Last week Saudi Arabia bought about 1.4 million tonnes of barley. Most of the barley was seen priced in the mid-$130s before freight and other costs.

Last week the European Union had granted only 5,000 tonnes of free-market barley at a subsidy of 27.14 Ecus per tonne, equating to an FOB price of $141, and 8,307 tonnes of German intervention barley at 106.55 Ecus, then worth $142 per tonne.

Traders, expecting the European Union would be eager to take the lion's share of the Saudi deal, had bid on Thursday through France to export 359,000 tonnes of free-market barley at refunds ranging from 28.80 to 36.65 Ecus per tonne.
Traders had placed no bids in Germany to export intervention or free-market barley due to a public holiday.
